title: Setting Up Your Environment
description: Install Node.js, npm, and create your first React project using Vite.

data.text: Before you can start building React applications, you need to set up your development environment. This involves installing Node.js, a package manager, and a build tool to create and run React projects.
**Node.js** is a JavaScript runtime that allows you to run JavaScript outside of a browser. It comes with **npm** (Node Package Manager), which you'll use to install React and other libraries.

items: Choose the LTS (Long Term Support) version for stability
Run the installer and follow the prompts
Verify installation by running `node -v` and `npm -v` in your terminal

data.text: Creating a React Project with Vite
**Vite** is a modern build tool that provides a faster and leaner development experience. It's the recommended way to start new React projects.

data.title: Create React App with Vite
data.code:
npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev

data.text: This creates a new React project in the `my-react-app` folder with everything you need to get started.
After creating your project, you'll see the following structure:

data.title: Project Structure
data.code:
my-react-app/
├── node_modules/
├── public/
├── src/
│   ├── App.css
│   ├── App.jsx
│   ├── index.css
│   └── main.jsx
├── index.html
├── package.json
└── vite.config.js

items: **index.html**: The HTML template that hosts your React app
**src/main.jsx**: The entry point that renders your app

data.text: Start the development server with `npm run dev`. This will start a local server (usually at `http://localhost:5173`) with hot module replacement, meaning your changes appear instantly in the browser.

data.title: Alternative: Create React App
data.text: While Vite is now recommended, you may still see Create React App (CRA) in older tutorials. CRA is slower but works the same way: `npx create-react-app my-app`

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Install Node.js to get npm and the JavaScript runtime
Use Vite to create new React projects quickly
Run `npm run dev` to start the development server
data.takeaway: Now that your environment is ready, let's learn about JSX, the syntax you'll use to write React components.
